summary: Dominik Wujastyk works in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of London and Oxford. His posts include the Wellcome Institute (~1984–2002), UCL (2002–2009), University of Vienna (2009–2015), and University of Alberta (2015).
Dominique Sportiche is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1979–1984). He held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles, beginning around 1988.
Dominique-Sila Khan was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Paris-Sorbonne University. She served as a research fellow at the Institute of Rajasthan Studies, attested in 2000.
Don A. Pittman works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed doctoral studies at the University of Chicago and served on the faculty at Texas Christian University, attested in 2001.

Don Handelman is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at McGill, Pittsburgh, and Manchester (~1967–1971), and served as Professor of Anthropology at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1972–2007).
Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied under Wilhelm Geiger at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from around 1894 to 1897.
Donald A. Ringe is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Bard College, Oxford, and Yale (~1978–1984), and joined the linguistics faculty at the University of Pennsylvania around 1985.

Donald Capps was a religious studies scholar who studied at Lewis & Clark College, Yale Divinity School, and the University of Chicago. He held posts at UNC Charlotte (~1976–1981) and Princeton Theological Seminary (~1981–2009).

Donald E. Gjertson worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Akira Takeda and completed his PhD under John Ching-yu Wang at Stanford (~1969–1975). He held a post at UMass Amherst (~1975–2012).

Donald K. Swearer is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He served at Swarthmore College (~1970–2004) and held posts at Harvard University as Distinguished Visiting Professor (2004–2010) and Distinguished Visiting Fellow (attested 2012).
Donald Phillip Verene is a philosopher who studied at Washington University in St. Louis (~1960–1964). He held a post at Emory University from around 1982 to 2021.
Donald R. Davis Jr. is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who studied under Richard W. Lariviere, Ludo Rocher, and Patrick Olivelle.

Donald S. Lopez Jr. works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, held posts at Middlebury College (~1979–1989), and joined the University of Michigan in 1990.
Dor Bahadur Bista is a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. He studied at Tri Chandra College (~1950–1954) and served as a professor at Tribhuvan University (~1972–1990).
Doranne Jacobson is an Indology scholar who earned a doctorate in anthropology at Columbia University, where she also served as a seminar associate at the Southern Asian Institute.
Doris Unterthurner is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed her MA at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Dorji Wangchuk is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his MA and PhD at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen, becoming a professor there around 2009.
Dorothy C. Wong works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She is a faculty member at the University of Virginia and was a visiting professor at the University of Hong Kong, attested in 2009.
Douglas Matthew Gildow is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Princeton University under the supervision of Stephen F. Teiser and Qi Zhou, attested in 2016.

Douglas Ober works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Washington and earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under Harjot Oberoi (~2011–2016).
